# Part IV. Strategic and Social Decisions {.unnumbered}

A team would benefit if everyone shared what they knew. Yet a member may stay quiet because speaking first seems risky, because others appear certain, or because the person who challenges the group usually pays a cost. A warning can disappear from the discussion while everyone takes the silence as agreement. The same silence can arise for different reasons; how can the team discover which one it needs to address?

Part IV starts with three examples that make strategic dependence visible: the outcome of a choice depends on what others do. They develop the problem of anticipating another person’s reasoning before introducing equilibrium. The next chapter makes those interactions explicit in payoff matrices and examines how shared expectations support coordination. We then ask what sustains cooperation when someone could gain by holding back. Later chapters turn to norms and social learning. Markets provide a larger setting in which individual forecasts become prices and those prices become information for later decisions.

The final chapters examine social influence and the meaning of agreement. A favor or earlier commitment can make a request harder to refuse; a title can make disagreement costly. Group discussion may leave unique information unshared, while culture or identity can change what silence means. Experiments help distinguish these influences, so that improving the decision begins with discovering why people are acting as they are.

[]{#fig-part-4-route}

## Questions to carry forward

- How does my best response depend on what others do?
- Which motives or beliefs could explain the same visible behavior?
- Can this group reveal disagreement and use information that only one member holds?

Social influence can change behavior without changing private belief, and can occur without anyone intending it. Part V turns to persuasion: how messages change beliefs and attitudes, and how conversation lets people check whether they have understood one another.
